label: Snap election called
description: Sánchez announces dissolution of the Cortes and an early general election for 29 November, after Congress rejected housing decree-laws 26/2026 and 27/2026.
hypothesis: Context; frames campaign around housing.

label: Urda rail crash
description: Collision of high-speed trains (AVE/Iryo) at Urda (Toledo) on the Madrid–Seville line; 69 dead. Date inferred from reports that victims were identified 'five days after' (3 Nov). CIS reports a small PSOE dip afterwards.
hypothesis: Retrospective punishment of the incumbent (PSOE down).

label: Transport minister Puente resigns
description: Óscar Puente resigns after the Adamuz (Jan 2026) and Urda rail accidents. Date from Wikipedia only; not confirmed by a news source.
hypothesis: Accountability signal; ambiguous effect on PSOE.

label: Zapatero stays charged (Plus Ultra)
description: Judge Calama rejects adding embezzlement charges but keeps former PM Zapatero under investigation for tax fraud and smuggling (Plus Ultra case).
hypothesis: Corruption salience hurts PSOE.

label: PP programme presented
description: PP presents its electoral programme.
hypothesis: Low salience; no detectable effect expected.

label: General strike on housing + police charges
description: First general strike in 14 years, on housing, wages and public services. Police charges and pepper spray against protesters; 1,144 incidents and 47 arrests (Interior). Turnout disputed.
hypothesis: Mobilises the left; may shift left voters from PSOE to Frente Amplio/Podemos (police repression under a PSOE government).

label: Zapatero investigation extended
description: Judge extends the Plus Ultra investigation of Zapatero to May 2027.
hypothesis: Corruption salience hurts PSOE (low salience).

label: Marlaska inquiry; Sánchez backs him
description: Marlaska orders an inquiry into the strike charges and bans tear gas; Sumar, Podemos and ERC demand his resignation; Sánchez defends him ('mi ojito izquierdo-derecho').
hypothesis: Left voters penalise PSOE; benefits Frente Amplio/Podemos.

label: Housing decrees vote
description: Diputación Permanente validates the first housing decree (rent extensions, eviction suspension) with PNV support and rejects the second (tenant compensation).
hypothesis: Housing salience; mixed signal for the government.

label: CIS macro-survey published
description: CIS pre-electoral survey (45,000 interviews) gives PSOE an 8-point lead and 134–143 seats; contradicts private polls showing a PP–Vox majority.
hypothesis: Bandwagon/underdog cues; mostly elite debate on CIS credibility.

label: Official campaign start + Vox programme
description: Campaign opens at midnight (pegada de carteles). Vox publishes a 55-page programme (deportations, 'national priority' in housing, repeal of gender laws).
hypothesis: Campaign activation increases partisan consolidation and reduces undecideds.

label: Jordi Wild interviews; Abascal cancels
description: YouTuber Jordi Wild releases interviews with Sánchez, Feijóo and Colau; Abascal cancels hours before recording, criticised even by Vox-friendly voices.
hypothesis: Young/online audiences; Vox may lose among young men.

label: laSexta economic debate
description: Second-tier debate on the economy (Cuerpo–PSOE, Bravo–PP, Figaredo–Vox, Bustinduy–Frente Amplio), moderated by Ana Pastor. No clear winner.
hypothesis: Small effects; possibly favours Frente Amplio visibility.

label: Attack on PP event in Hernani
description: About 200 people throw bottles, firecrackers and eggs at a PP information tent in Hernani (Gipuzkoa); PP candidate Jon Echeverría escorted out. Containers burned near San Mamés (Bilbao) the same day.
hypothesis: Sympathy/rally effect for PP; polarisation on Basque issue.

label: Record boat arrivals in the Canary Islands
description: Weekend of 14–15 Nov: reported record arrivals (3,684 people per a press-release aggregator; 11,037 in first half of November per Interior). Combines with ongoing Ceuta crisis debate.
hypothesis: Immigration salience benefits Vox.

label: PSOE programme; Sánchez calls Abascal 'racist'
description: PSOE presents 'La fuerza de la gente' in Alcorcón (1% of GDP to housing, paid childcare leave, tax on large owners of empty flats). In La Séptima Sánchez calls Abascal 'racista'. Begoña Gómez appears at Seville rally.
hypothesis: Mobilises PSOE base; polarisation PSOE–Vox.

label: Lula at Moncloa; Frente Amplio programme; CNI on Ceuta
description: Lula and Orsí visit Moncloa (rally cancelled). Frente Amplio presents its programme; Yolanda Díaz attends Colau's housing event. CNI tells the Audiencia there is no evidence of Moroccan involvement in the Ceuta mass entry. Abascal rally in Tenerife on immigration.
hypothesis: Small effects; Frente Amplio visibility; immigration salience for Vox.

label: Sánchez Telecinco interview (Ceuta holidays)
description: Tense interview with Carlos Franganillo on the Ceuta crisis and Sánchez's holidays at La Mareta; Sánchez announces public-sector pay rise for the next day. Some outlets date it 17 Nov.
hypothesis: Negative coverage for PSOE on immigration/Ceuta.

label: Public-sector pay rise and minimum wage increase approved
description: Council of Ministers approves a 4.5% pay rise for civil servants in 2027 (part of an 11% 2025-2028 deal) and raises the minimum wage (SMI) by 5.3% to 1,286 euros a month in 14 payments. PP calls it partisan use of the Council of Ministers during the campaign.
hypothesis: Incumbent benefits (public employees).

label: Abascal's wife receives heating subsidy for vulnerable families
description: infoLibre reports that Lidia Bedman, Abascal's wife, received the bono social térmico (210 euros, paid by the Comunidad de Madrid) as a large family. It is legal (no income limit for large families) but clashes with Vox's attacks on 'paguitas'. In Arrecife Abascal defends it as 'de justicia' and says public money is better with families than with Sánchez's friends, 'que se lo gastan en putas y mordidas'.
hypothesis: Hypocrisy frame hurts Vox and Abascal; the crude remark may mobilise both sides.

label: Feijóo interview on the podcast El sentido de la birra
description: Recorded days earlier and released on 18 Nov, after The Wild Project. Feijóo says Vox has set him no red lines, defends the understanding with Abascal, backs 'total or partial' repeal of the euthanasia law while guaranteeing abortion and LGTBI rights, and criticises Sánchez for declining the same podcast.
hypothesis: Open talk of a PP-Vox deal could mobilise the left; outreach to young voters may help the PP among them.

label: Sánchez interview on Antena 3 (Espejo Público)
description: Sánchez is interviewed by Susanna Griso on Espejo Público, two days after the Telecinco interview; he declined invitations from Ana Rosa Quintana and Pablo Motos.
hypothesis: Low salience; no detectable effect expected.

label: Diputación Permanente validates seven decree-laws
description: The Diputación Permanente validates seven decree-laws: aid for Ceuta (45 million euros), the DANA Adam floods and the Urda crash victims, rail safety, Social Security benefits, single-parent families and dependency care. PP votes for all seven; Vox backs only the Urda aid.
hypothesis: Low salience; no detectable effect expected.

label: Puigdemont interview in El Mundo
description: El Mundo publishes an interview recorded in Waterloo in which Puigdemont describes the 2023 Junts-PSOE negotiations: 'nos hemos aprovechado de la ambición desmedida de Sánchez para derrotar a España'. Turull endorses it; Nicolás Redondo says he will not vote PSOE.
hypothesis: Salience of the Catalan pacts hurts PSOE and helps PP and Vox.

label: Police report: Ceuta mass entry was planned
description: A National Police (CENIF) report sent to the Audiencia Nacional concludes that the July mass entry into Ceuta (100,000-125,000 people) had prior logistics, citing 8,000-10,000 identical swim rings. It contrasts with the CNI report (16 Nov) that found no evidence of Moroccan involvement, which Sánchez cites in the debate that evening.
hypothesis: Immigration and Ceuta salience; hurts PSOE, helps Vox and PP.

label: Sánchez–Feijóo head-to-head debate
description: Only head-to-head debate of the campaign, organised by the Academia de la Televisión and moderated by María Casado (22:00-23:40; five blocks: housing, economy, social policy, corruption, migration). Feijóo presses Sánchez to apologise to the Urda and Adamuz rail victims, and Sánchez agrees; they clash on Ceuta and Morocco. A SocioMétrica poll for El Español: 64% say Feijóo won, 32% Sánchez.
hypothesis: Debate winner gains: PP and Feijóo up, PSOE and Sánchez down.

label: Train drivers call off strike (Semaf)
description: Semaf calls off the 23 Nov strike at Renfe and Adif after an agreement with the Transport Ministry and Renfe on rail safety (adverse-weather protocol signed on 19 Nov, 110 million euros for train air conditioning). CCOO, UGT and SCF had suspended their Adif strike on 18 Nov; CSIF keeps protesting.
hypothesis: Removes a source of rail chaos; low salience, no detectable effect expected.

label: Supreme Court bars 'ley de nietos' citizens from voting
description: The Supreme Court orders the Junta Electoral Central to keep 163,355 people naturalised under the 'ley de nietos' (Democratic Memory Law) off the electoral roll on 29 Nov, now including those living in Spain, unless they prove descent from exiles. Vox and Iustitia Europa had challenged the INE's compliance report.
hypothesis: Low salience for the electorate; no detectable effect expected.

label: Poll publication ban starts
description: Legal ban on publishing polls (24–28 Nov).

label: Four-way leaders' debate
description: Academia de la Televisión debate with Sánchez, Feijóo, Abascal and Colau, three days before the vote. On 20 Nov the Junta Electoral Central confirmed that Podemos is not included.
hypothesis: Debate effects on all four parties.

label: Election day
description: General election.
